1001.text: Calculate molarity of $63 \% \mathrm{w} / \mathrm{w} \mathrm{HNO}_3$ solution if density is $1.4 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mL}$.
1001.sol:
$63 \%$ nitric acid by mass means that mass of nitric acid $=63 \mathrm{~g}$
Mass of solution $=100 \mathrm{~g}$
Molar mass of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=63 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
Mole of $\mathrm{HNO}_3=\frac{63 \mathrm{~g}}{63 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}=1 \mathrm{~mole}$
Density of solution $=1.4 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}\therefore \quad$ Volume of solution
$=\frac{100 \mathrm{~g}}{1.4 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}}=71.428 \mathrm{~mL}=0.071428 \mathrm{~L}$
Molarity of solution $=\frac{\text{ Moles of solute }}{\text{ Volume of solution in } \mathrm{L}} =\frac{1.0}{0.071428} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}=14 \mathrm{M}$

3044.text:
For the gaseous reactions (I) and (II), the equilibrium constants are $X$ and $Y$ respectively.
I. $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_2(g)$
II. $2 \mathrm{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(g)$
Using the above reactions the equilibrium constant $Z$ for the reaction (III) given below is
III. $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(g)+2 \mathrm{O}_2(g)$
3044.sol: For reaction $\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ N}_2(g)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) & \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_2(g) \\ X & =K_{C_1}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]}{\left[\mathrm{N}_2\right]^{1 / 2}\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]} \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \text{$ For $} 2 \mathrm{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(g) \\ & Y=K_{C_2}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right]}{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}\end{aligned}$ For reaction $\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{N}_2(g)+2 \mathrm{O}_2$ Substituting values from equation (i) and (ii) in equation (iii) we get. $\begin{aligned} & Z=\left(\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]}{X}\right)^2 / Y\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2 \\ & Z=\frac{\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}{X^2 Y\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]^2}=\frac{1}{X^2 Y} \end{aligned}$

3305.text: In which of the following, elements are arranged in the correct order of their electron gain enthalpies.

We know that the electron gain enthalpy increases from left to right and decreases from top to bottom. So here, Fluorine& has maximum electron gain enthalpy. $F > S > O > N$

6645.subject: Mathematics
6645.text: The coefficient of $x^4$ in the power series expansion of $\frac{x^2-1}{\left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^2+2\right)}$ is
6645.sol:
Using binomial expansions,

$$\begin{aligned}& \frac{\left(x^2-1\right)}{ \left(x^2+1\right)\left(x^2+2\right)}=\ffrac{1}{2}\left(x^2-1\right) \left(1+x^2\right)^{-1}\lleft(1+\frac{x^2}{2}\right)^{-1}\\
=  \frac{1}{2}\left[\left(x^2-1\right)\left(1-x²+x⁴ \ldots\right) \lleft(1-\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{x^4}{4} \ldots\right)\right]\\
= & \frac{1}{2}\left[\left(x^2-1\right)\lleft(1-\frac{x^2}{2}+\ffrac{x^4}{4}-x²+\frac{x^4}{2}+x^4 \ldots\right)\right] \\
= & \frac{1}{2}\left[ \left(x²-1\right)\lleft(1-\ffrac{3}{2}x^2+\frac{7}{4} x^4 \ldots\right)\right] \\
= & \frac{1}{2}\lleft[-1+\ffrac{3}{2}x^2-\f frac{7}{4}x^4+x²-\frac{3}{2}x^4 \ldots\right]
\end{aligned}$$

taking coefficient of $x^4$,

$=\frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{7}{4}-\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{-13}{4}\right)=\frac{-13}{8} $$\text{. }$

Given, $f ( x ) = \dfrac{cotx}{1 + cotx}$ and $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{5\pi}{4}$

$⇒ cot\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = cot\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cot \alpha cot \beta - 1}{cot \beta + cot \alpha} = 1$

$⇒ cot \alpha cot \beta = 1 + cot \beta + cot \alpha$

Now, $f\left(\alpha\right) = \dfrac{cot\alpha}{1 + cot\alpha}, f\left(\beta\right) = \dfrac{cot\beta}{1 + cot \beta}$

Then, $f\left(\alpha\right)f\left(\beta\right) = \dfrac{cot\alpha}{1 + cot\alpha} \times \dfrac{cot\beta}{1 + cot \beta}$

$= \dfrac{cot\alphacot\beta}{1 + cot \alpha cot \beta + cot\alpha + cot \beta}$

$= \dfrac{cot\alphacot\beta}{2cot \alpha cot \beta}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}$

19754.subject: Chemistry
19754.text:
Arrange the following in the increasing order of their covalent character.
$\mathrm{CaF}_2 ; \mathrm{CaCl}_2 ; \mathrm{CaBr}_2 ; \mathrm{CaI}_2$
19754.sol:
According to Fajan's rule, the covalent character in ionic compounds increases with the increase in the polarizability of the anion. The polarizability of an anion depends on its size; larger anions are more easily polarized by the cation.

The cations in all the given compounds are the same, which is $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$. The anions are $\mathrm{F}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$, $\mathrm{Br}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{I}^{-}$.

The size of the halide ions increases in the order: $\mathrm{F}^{-} < \mathrm{Cl}^{-} < \mathrm{Br}^{-} < \mathrm{I}^{-}$.

Since the polarizability increases as the size of the anion increases, the covalent character follows the order of the size of the anions. Therefore, the increasing order of covalent character is $\mathrm{CaF}_2 < \mathrm{CaCl}_2 < \mathrm{CaBr}_2 < \mathrm{CaI}_2$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CaF}_2 < \mathrm{CaCl}_2 < \mathrm{CaBr}_2 < \mathrm{CaI}_2$

20546.subject: Chemistry
options: Calcium and Magnesium metals are manufactured by electrolysis of aqueous solutions of their salts
The oxo-anion $\mathrm{ClO}_3^{-}$ does not undergo disproportionation reaction
Nitride ion \(\mathrm{N}^{-3}\) cannot act as an oxidising agent
In alkaline medium the reduction of $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$ ion involves gain of 5 electrons
20546.sol:
Calcium and Magnesium are highly reactive metals with standard reduction potentials more negative than that of water. Electrolysis of their aqueous salt solutions results in the evolution of hydrogen gas at the cathode rather than the deposition of the metal. Therefore, they are manufactured by the electrolysis of their molten chloride salts.

The chlorate ion $\mathrm{ClO}_{3}^{-}$ contains chlorine in the $+5$ oxidation state. It can undergo disproportionation into chloride ($-1$) and perchlorate ($+7$) ions, especially in acidic or basic conditions, making the statement that it does not undergo disproportionation incorrect.

The nitride ion $\mathrm{N}^{3-}$ has nitrogen in its lowest possible oxidation state of $-3$. Since it cannot be reduced further, it cannot act as an oxidizing agent. It can only act as a reducing agent by losing electrons to form nitrogen gas or other nitrogen-containing species.

In an alkaline medium, the reduction of the permanganate ion $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ (where Mn is $+7$) typically proceeds to the manganate ion $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ (where Mn is $+6$), which involves a gain of 1 electron, or to manganese dioxide $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}$ (where Mn is $+4$), which involves a gain of 3 electrons. The gain of 5 electrons occurs in an acidic medium where $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$.

Answer: Nitride ion \(\mathrm{N}^{-3}\) cannot act as an oxidising agent

20939.subject: Mathematics
20939.text: The points on the ellipse $16 x^2+9 y^2=400$ at which the ordinate decreases at the same rate at which the abscissa increases are
20939.sol: The given equation of the ellipse is $16x^2 + 9y^2 = 400$.Differentiating both sides with respect to time $t$, we get $32x \dfrac{dx}{dt} + 18y \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$.The problem states that the ordinate decreases at the same rate at which the abscissa increases, which means $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.Substituting this into the differentiated equation: $32x \dfrac{dx}{dt} + 18y \left(-\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right) = 0$.Assuming $\dfrac{dx}{dt} \neq 0$, we have $32x - 18y = 0$, which simplifies to $16x = 9y$, or $y = \dfrac{16x}{9}$.Substitute $y = \dfrac{16x}{9}$ into the original ellipse equation: $16x^2 + 9 \left(\dfrac{16x}{9}\right)^2 = 400$.$16x^2 + 9 \left(\dfrac{256x^2}{81}\right) = 400$.$16x^2 + \dfrac{256x^2}{9} = 400$.Multiplying by $9$: $144x^2 + 256x^2 = 3600$.$400x^2 = 3600$, so $x^2 = 9$, which gives $x = 3 or x = -3$.If $x = 3$, $y = \dfrac{16(3)}{9} = \dfrac{16}{3}$.If $x = -3$, $y = \dfrac{16(-3)}{9} = -\dfrac{16}{3}$.The points are $\left(3, \dfrac{16}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-3, -\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$.Answer: $\left(3, \dfrac{16}{3}\right) \text{$ and }$\left(-3,-\dfrac{16}{3}\right)$

21098.text: Number of terms in the binomial expansion of $(x+a)^{53}+(x-a)^{53}$ is
21098.sol:
The expansion of $(x+a)^{n} + (x-a)^{n}$ is given by $2[^{n}C_{0}x^{n} + ^{n}C_{2}x^{n-2}a^{2} + ^{n}C_{4}x^{n-4}a^{4} + \dots]$.

For $n = 53$, the expansion is $(x+a)^{53} + (x-a)^{53} = 2[^{53}C_{0}x^{53} + ^{53}C_{2}x^{51}a^{2} + \dots + ^{53}C_{52}x^{1}a^{52}]$.

The terms in the expansion correspond to the values of $k$ in ^{53}C_{2k}x^{53-2k}a^{2k}$ where 2k$ ranges from $0$ to $52$.

The possible values for $k$ are $0, 1, 2, \dots, 26$.

The total number of terms is the number of values in the set $\{0, 1, 2, \dots, 26\}$, which is $26 - 0 + 1 = 27$.

Answer: 27

21248.sol:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\cos x}{1 + \cos x + \sin x}dx$... (1)

Using $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)dx$, substitute $x \to \dfrac{\pi}{2} - x$:

$I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \sin x + \cos x}dx$... (2)

Adding (1) and (2):

$2I = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\cos x + \sin x}{1 + \cos x + \sin x}dx = \int_0^{\pi/2} \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos x + \sin x}\right)dx$

$2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - J$ where $J = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{1 + \cos x + \sin x}dx$

Using half-angle: $\cos x = 2\cos^2\dfrac{x}{2} - 1$, $\sin x = 2\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\cos\dfrac{x}{2}$:

$J = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{2\cos^2\frac{x}{2} + 2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}}dx$

Dividing by $2\cos^2\dfrac{x}{2}$:

$J = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}}{1 + \tan\frac{x}{2}}dx$

Let $t = 1 + \tan\dfrac{x}{2}$, $dt = \dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\dfrac{x}{2}dx$. Limits: $t: 1 \to 2$

$J = \displaystyle\int_1^2 \dfrac{1}{t}dt = \log 2$

$2I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \log 2 \Rightarrow I = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{1}{2}\log 2$

21338.subject: Mathematics
21338.text: Degree of the differential equation $\log \left(\dfrac{d y}{d x}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}=5 x+4 y$ is
21338.sol:
The given differential equation is $\log \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 5x + 4y$.

Removing the logarithm by taking the exponential of both sides, we get $\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^{\dfrac{1}{2}} = e^{5x+4y}$.

Squaring both sides to eliminate the fractional exponent, we obtain $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (e^{5x+4y})^2 = e^{10x+8y}$.

The differential equation is now in the form $f(x, y, y') = 0$, where $y' = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$. The highest order derivative present is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, which is of order 1. The power of the highest order derivative in the polynomial form is 1. Therefore, the degree of the differential equation is 1.

Answer: 1

21688.text: $\text{ The maximum value of } Z=3 x+4 y \text{ for the given constraints } x+2 y \leq 76,2 x+y \leq 104, x \geq 0, y \geq 0 \text{$ is }
21688.sol:
The constraints are $x + 2y \leq 76$, $2x + y \leq 104$, $x \geq 0$, and $y \geq 0$.

The corner points of the feasible region are found by solving the intersection of the boundary lines and the axes.

1. Intersection of $x + 2y = 76$ and $2x + y = 104$:
Multiply the first equation by 2: $2x + 4y = 152$.
Subtract the second equation: $(2x + 4y) - (2x + y) = 152 - 104 \Rightarrow 3y = 48 \Rightarrow y = 16$.
Substitute $y = 16$ into $x + 2(16) = 76 \Rightarrow x + 32 = 76 \Rightarrow x = 44$.
Corner point: $(44,16)$.

2. Intersection of $x + 2y = 76$ with the y-axis (x=0$):
2y = 76 \Rightarrow y = 38$.
Corner point: $(0,38)$.

3. Intersection of $2x + y = 104$ with the x-axis (y=0$):
2x = 104 \Rightarrow x = 52$.
Corner point: $(52,0)$.

4. Origin: $(0,0)$.

Evaluate $Z = 3x + 4y$ at each corner point:
At $(0,0)$: $Z = 3(0) + 4(0) = 0$.
At $(0,38)$: $Z = 3(0) + 4(38) = 152$.
At $(52,0)$: $Z = 3(52) + 4(0) = 156$.
At $(44,16)$: $Z = 3(44) + 4(16) = 132 + 64 = 196$.

The maximum value is 196.

Answer: 196

21887.subject: Mathematics
21887.text: If for two events $A$ and $B, P(A-B)=\dfrac{1}{5}$ and $P(A)=\dfrac{3}{5}$ then $P(B / A)=$
21887.sol:
The probability of the event $A-B$ is given by $P(A-B) = P(A) - P(A \cap B)$.

Given $P(A-B) = \dfrac{1}{5}$ and $P(A) = \dfrac{3}{5}$, we substitute these values into the equation:

$\dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{3}{5} - P(A \cap B)$

$P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{3}{5} - \dfrac{1}{5} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

The conditional probability $P(B/A)$ is defined as $P(B/A) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)}$.

Substituting the known values:

$P(B/A) = \dfrac{2/5}{3/5} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}$

22124.sol: Let the line pass through the point $P(1, 2)$ at an angle $\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis. The equation of the line in parametric form is $\dfrac{x-1}{\cos \theta} = \dfrac{y-2}{\sin \theta} = r$, where $r$ is the distance from $P$.Any point on this line is given by $(1 + r \cos \theta, 2 + r \sin \theta)$.The intersection point lies on the line $x + y = 4$. Substituting the coordinates of the point into this equation:$(1 + r \cos \theta) + (2 + r \sin \theta) = 4 3 + r(\cos \theta + \sin \theta) = 4 r(\cos \theta + \sin \theta) = 1$Given $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$, we have $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}(\cos \theta + \sin \theta) = 1$.$\cos \theta + \sin \theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$.Multiplying by $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ on both sides:$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cos \theta + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sin \theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.$\sin(\theta + 45^{{}^{\circ}}) = \sin 60^{{}^{\circ}}$ or $\sin(\theta + 45^{{}^{\circ}}) = \sin 120^{{}^{\circ}}$.Case 1: $\theta + 45^{{}^{\circ}} = 60^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \theta = 15^{{}^{\circ}}$.Case 2: $\theta + 45^{{}^{\circ}} = 120^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow \theta = 75^{{}^{\circ}}$.Thus, the required angles are $15^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $75^{{}^{\circ}}$.Answer: $15^{{}^{\circ}} \text{ or } 75^{{}^{\circ}}$

22167.subject: Mathematics
22167.text: The angle between the two lines whose direction cosines satisfy the relations $l + m + n = 0$ and $l^2 = m^2 + n^2$ is
22167.sol:
Given the relations $l + m + n = 0$ and $l^2 = m^2 + n^2$.

From the first equation, we have $l = -(m + n)$.

Substituting this into the second equation:

$(-(m + n))^2 = m^2 + n^2$

$m^2 + n^2 + 2mn = m^2 + n^2$

$2mn = 0$

This gives either $m = 0$ or $n = 0$.

Case 1: If $m = 0$, then $l = -n$. The direction ratios of the first line are proportional to $(-n, 0, n)$, which simplifies to $(-1, 0, 1)$.

Case 2: If $n = 0$, then $l = -m$. The direction ratios of the second line are proportional to $(-m, m, 0)$, which simplifies to $(-1, 1, 0)$.

The angle $\theta$ between the two lines is given by:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 + c_1 c_2|}{\sqrt{a_1^2 + b_1^2 + c_1^2} \sqrt{a_2^2 + b_2^2 + c_2^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|(-1)(-1) + (0)(1) + (1)(0)|}{\sqrt{(-1)^2 + 0^2 + 1^2} \sqrt{(-1)^2 + 1^2 + 0^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

24906.text: Correct statement(s) about the compounds $\textbf{P}$, $\textbf{Q}$ and $\textbf{R}$ is(are)
options: $\textbf{P}$ has two lone pairs of electrons on the central atom.
$\textbf{Q}$ can act as a fluorinating agent.
The molecular structure of $\textbf{R}$ is trigonal pyramidal.
24906.sol:
From the given reaction conditions:

$\text{Xe(g)} + 2\text{F}_2\text{(g)} \xrightarrow[\text{1 : 5 ratio}]{\text{873 K, 7 bar}} \text{XeF}_4$
Thus, $\textbf{P}$ is $\text{XeF}_4$.

$\text{XeF}_4 + \text{O}_2\text{F}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{143 K}} \text{XeF}_6 + \text{O}_2$
Thus, $\textbf{Q}$ is $\text{XeF}_6$.

$\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{complete hydrolysis}} \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$
Thus, $\textbf{R}$ is $\text{XeO}_3$.

Evaluating the given options:
(A) $\textbf{P}$ ($\text{XeF}_4$) has $8$ valence electrons on the central Xe atom. It forms $4$ single bonds with F, leaving $4$ electrons which form $2$ lone pairs. This statement is correct.

(B) $\textbf{Q}$ ($\text{XeF}_6$) has $6$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair on the central Xe atom. Its geometry is distorted octahedral, not perfect octahedral. This statement is incorrect.

(C) $\textbf{Q}$ ($\text{XeF}_6$) is a strong fluorinating agent. This statement is correct.

(D) $\textbf{R}$ ($\text{XeO}_3$) has $3$ double bonds and $1$ lone pair on the central Xe atom. Its molecular structure is trigonal pyramidal. This statement is correct.

Answer: $\textbf{P}$ has two lone pairs of electrons on the central atom.; $\textbf{Q}$ can act as a fluorinating agent.; The molecular structure of $\textbf{R}$ is trigonal pyramidal.

For the reaction, ${A}_{2}\overset{{K}_{1}}{\to}2A$

${r}_{f} = - \dfrac{d\left[{A}_{2}\right]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{1} = {K}_{1}\left[{A}_{2}\right]$

${\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{1} = 2{K}_{1}\left[{A}_{2}\right]$

${r}_{b} = - \dfrac{1}{2}{\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{2} = {K}_{- 1}{\left[A\right]}^{2}$

${\left(\dfrac{d\left[A\right]}{dt}\right)}_{2} = - 2{K}_{- 1}{\left[A\right]}^{2}$

Hence, the overall rate is given by:

30247.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement - I: High concentration of strong nucleophilic reagent with secondary alkyl halides which do not have bulky substituents will follow ${S}_{N}2$ mechanism.
Statement - II: A secondary alkyl halide when treated with a large excess of ethanol follows ${S}_{N}1$ mechanism.
In the the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the questions given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both statement I and Statement II are false.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.
30247.sol:
Statement - I: Rate of ${S}_{N}2 ∝ [ R - X ] \left[{Nu}^{-}\right]
${S}_{N}2 reaction $is favoured by high concentration of nucleophile \left({Nu}^{-}\right)\text{ and } less crowding in the substrate molecule.$

${S}_{N}2$ Reaction Mechanism

This reaction proceeds through a backside attack by the nucleophile on the substrate. The nucleophile approaches the given substrate at an angle of ${180}^{°}$ to the carbon-leaving group bond. The carbon-nucleophile bond forms and carbon-leaving group bond breaks simultaneously through a transition state.$

Now, the leaving group is pushed out of the transition state on the opposite side of the carbon-nucleophile bond, forming the required product. It is important to note that the product is formed with an inversion of the tetrahedral geometry at the atom in the centre.

Statement - II: Solvolysis follows ${S}_{N}1$ path.$

he ${S}_{N}1$ reaction is a nucleophilic substitution reaction where the rate-determining step is unimolecular. It is a type of organic substitution reaction. ${S}_{N}1$ stands for substitution nucleophilic unimolecular. Thus, the rate equation (which states that the ${S}_{N}1$ reaction is dependent on the electrophile but not on the nucleophile) holds in situations where the amount of the nucleophile is far greater than the amount of the carbocation intermediate.$

This reaction involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate. It is generally seen in the reactions of tertiary or secondary alkyl halides with secondary or tertiary alcohols under strongly acidic or strongly basic conditions. The ${S}_{N}1$ reaction is often referred to as the dissociative mechanism in inorganic chemistry.$

Both are correct statements.

30401.subject: Chemistry
30401.text: An alkene $(X)$ on ozonolysis followed by reduction gives following products: $H-CHO$ ($2$ moles), $H-CO-CO-CHO$, $CH_3-CO-CO-CH_3$. The alkene $(X)$ is:
30401.sol:
Ozonolysis (followed by reductive workup with $Zn/H_2O$) cleaves $C=C$ bonds and converts each alkene carbon into a carbonyl. We can reverse-engineer the parent alkene from the fragments obtained.

Analysing the products:
$HCHO$ $(2\text{ moles})$: Two equivalents of formaldehyde indicate the presence of two terminal or exocyclic $=CH_2$ groups in the parent molecule.

$CH_3-CO-CO-CH_3$ (biacetyl): To get this discrete fragment, the parent alkene must contain the structural unit $-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-$, i.e., an endocyclic double bond in which both sp$^2$ carbons bear methyl substituents.

$H-CO-CO-CHO$ (mesoxaldehyde): This arises from a fragment like $=CH-C(=CH_2)-CH=$, where cleavage of the adjacent $C=C$ bonds generates three consecutive carbonyl groups (and also contributes to the formaldehyde count from the exocyclic $=CH_2$).

Evaluating the options:
The most diagnostic product is biacetyl, so the parent structure must contain the $-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-$ unit.

Option $(1)$: One methyl group is on the endocyclic double bond and the other methyl is on a separate sp$^3$ carbon. Cleavage cannot give biacetyl.

Option $(2)$: Only a single methyl group is present, so biacetyl cannot be formed.

Option $(4)$: The methyl groups lie on opposite ends of the ring (across a $1,4$-diene-type arrangement). Ozonolysis would place these methyls in different fragments, so biacetyl cannot be formed.

Option $(3)$: The left side of the ring contains an endocyclic double bond in which both carbons carry methyl groups, giving exactly the required $-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-$ arrangement. Cleavage of this bond together with the adjacent ring double bonds releases a discrete $CH_3-CO-CO-CH_3$ fragment. The right side of the molecule carries exocyclic $=CH_2$ groups, which on cleavage produce the two moles of $HCHO$, while the intervening carbons give rise to $H-CO-CO-CHO$.

Hence, the correct structure that yields all three ozonolysis products is option $(3)$.

31263.text: A salt with few drops of conc. HCl gives apple green colour in flame test. The group precipitate of the salt is dissolved in acetic acid and treated with $K_2CrO_4$ to give yellow precipitate. When the sodium carbonate extract of the salt solution is heated with conc. $HNO_3$ and ammonium molybdate, it resulted a canary yellow precipitate. The cation and anion present in the salt are respectively,
31263.sol:
An apple green colour in the flame test indicates the presence of $Ba^{2+}$ ion.

The group precipitate of $Ba^{2+}$ is $BaCO_3$, which dissolves in acetic acid to form barium acetate. Upon treatment with $K_2CrO_4$, it gives a yellow precipitate of barium chromate ($BaCrO_4$), confirming the presence of $Ba^{2+}$.

When the sodium carbonate extract is heated with conc. $HNO_3$ and ammonium molybdate, the formation of a canary yellow precipitate indicates the presence of phosphate ($PO_4^{3-}$) ion. The canary yellow precipitate is ammonium phosphomolybdate, $(NH_4)_3PO_4 \cdot 12MoO_3$.

Therefore, the cation is $Ba^{2+}$ and the anion is $PO_4^{3-}$.

Answer: $Ba^{2+}$ and $PO_4^{3-}$

31325.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: ${S}_{8}$ solid undergoes disproportionation reaction under alkaline conditions to form ${S}^{2 -}$ and ${S}_{2}{O}_{3}^{2 -}$

Statement II: ${ClO}_{4}^{-}$ can undergo disproportionation reaction under acidic condition.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct
31325.sol:
A disproportionation reaction is a reaction in which the same element is simultaneously oxidized and reduced. In this type of reaction, a single substance gives two products, one is oxidized while the other is reduced.

${S}_{1}: {S}_{8} + 12{OH}^{⊝} \to 4{S}^{2 -} + 2{S}_{2}{O}_{3}^{2 -} + 6{H}_{2}O$

${S}_{2}: {ClO}_{4}^{⊝}$ cannot undergo disproportionation reaction as chlorine is present in its highest oxidation state.

Hence, statement $I$ is correct and $II$ is incorrect.

33746.text: Let $S = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : z^2 + \sqrt{6}\,iz - 3 = 0\}$. Then $\sum\limits_{z \in S} z^8$ is equal to :
33746.sol:
Given equation is $z^2 + \sqrt{6}iz - 3 = 0$.

Rearranging the terms, we get $z^2 - 3 = -\sqrt{6}iz$.

Squaring both sides, we obtain:

$(z^2 - 3)^2 = (-\sqrt{6}iz)^2$

$z^4 - 6z^2 + 9 = -6z^2$

$z^4 + 9 = 0$

$z^4 = -9$

Squaring again, we get:

$(z^4)^2 = (-9)^2$

$z^8 = 81$

Since the given equation is a quadratic in $z$, it has two roots, say $z_1$ and $z_2$.

The discriminant of the quadratic equation is $\Delta = (\sqrt{6}i)^2 - 4(1)(-3) = -6 + 12 = 6 \neq 0$, which means the roots are distinct.

Thus, the set $S$ contains two distinct elements $z_1$ and $z_2$.

For each root, $z^8 = 81$.

Therefore, $\sum\limits_{z \in S} z^8 = z_1^8 + z_2^8 = 81 + 81 = 162$.

Answer: $162$

34834.text: The solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y = {x}^{2}, ( x \ne 0 )$ with $y\left(1\right) = 1$, is
34834.sol:
Given, differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{2}{x}\right)y = x$

This is a linear differential equation of type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P \text{ and } Q$ are the functions of $x$ or constants.

Thus, $P = \dfrac{2}{x} \text{ and } Q = x$

The integrating factor $I . F . = {e}^{∫ Pdx}$

$= {e}^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = {e}^{2lnx}$

$= {e}^{ln{x}^{2}} = {x}^{2} .$

The solution of the linear differential equation is $y \times \left(I . F .\right) = ∫ \left(Q \times I . F .\right)dx + C$

So, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y{x}^{2} = ∫ x \cdot {x}^{2}dx + C$

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = ∫ {x}^{3}dx + C$

Using $∫ {x}^{n}dx = \dfrac{{x}^{n + 1}}{n + 1},$ we get

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} + C$

Since $y\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 \cdot 1 = \dfrac{1}{4} + C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ {x}^{2}y = \dfrac{{x}^{4}}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{3}{4{x}^{2}} .$

42551.subject: Physics
42551.text: Two radioactive materials $A$ and $B$ have decay constants $25\lambda$ and $16\lambda$ respectively. If initially they have the same number of nuclei, then the ratio of the number of nuclei of $B$ to that of A will be "$e$" after a time $\dfrac{1}{a\lambda}$. The value of $a$ is _____ .
42551.sol:
According to radioactive decay formula, $N = {N}_{0}{e}^{- \lambdat}$, here, ${N}_{0}$ is the initial number of nuclei in a radioactive material.

Given here, ${\lambda}_{1} = 25\lambda$ and ${\lambda}_{2} = 16\lambda$.

And $\dfrac{{N}_{B}}{{N}_{A}} = e$

For radioactive material $A$, ${N}_{A} = {N}_{0}{e}^{- {\lambda}_{1}t}$

For radioactive material $B$, ${N}_{B} = {N}_{0}{e}^{- {\lambda}_{2}t}$

Thus, the ratio $\dfrac{{N}_{B}}{{N}_{A}} = \dfrac{{e}^{- {\lambda}_{2}t}}{{e}^{- {\lambda}_{1}t}} = {e}^{- {\lambda}_{2}t} \cdot {e}^{{\lambda}_{1}t}$

$⇒ {e}^{1} = {e}^{\left({\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2}\right)t}$

$⇒ \left({\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2}\right)t = 1$

Time, $t = \dfrac{1}{{\lambda}_{1} - {\lambda}_{2}} = \dfrac{1}{25\lambda - 16\lambda} = \dfrac{1}{9\lambda}$.

Hence, the value of $a = 9$.

44437.subject: Physics
44437.text:
A tunning fork of frequency $340Hz$ resonates in the fundamental mode with an air column of length $125cm$ in a cylindrical tube closed at one end. When water is slowly poured in it, the minimum height of water required for observing resonance once again is _____ $cm$.
(Velocity of sound in air is $340{ms}^{- 1}$)
44437.sol:
We know that, $v = \lambdaf$, then, $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{340m{s}^{- 1}}{340Hz} = \dfrac{340m{s}^{- 1}}{340{s}^{- 1}} = 1m$

First resonating length, ${l}_{1} = \dfrac{\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{100}{4} = 25cm$

Second resonating length, ${l}_{2} = \dfrac{3\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{3 \times 100}{4} = 75cm$

Third resonating length, ${l}_{3} = \dfrac{5\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{5 \times 100}{4} = 125cm$

So third resonance is not possible since the length of the tube is $125cm$

Thus, minimum height of water necessary for resonance $= 125 - 75 = 50cm$

46407.text: Two wire of same material having radius in ratio $2: 1$ and lengths in ratio $1: 2$. If same force is applied on them, then ratio of their change in length will be
46407.sol:
Given, ratio of radius of two wires $r_1: r_2=2: 1 \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}=\frac{2}{1}$
and ratio in their lengths, $1_1: 1_2=1: 2 \Rightarrow \quad \frac{l_1}{1_2}=\frac{1}{2}$
When same force is applied on them, then ratio r change in their length $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{l}_2}=$ ?
We know that, Young's modulus
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Y}=\frac{\mathrm{Fl}}{\mathrm{A} \Delta \mathrm{l}} \Rightarrow \Delta \mathrm{l}=\frac{\mathrm{Fl}}{\mathrm{AY}} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{l} \propto \frac{1}{\mathrm{~A}} \\
\therefore \quad & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{I}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{I}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1}{\mathrm{~A}_1} / \frac{\mathrm{l}_2}{\mathrm{~A}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1 \mathrm{~A}_2}{\mathrm{l}_2 \mathrm{~A}_1} \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}_1}{\Delta \mathrm{I}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{l}_1}{\mathrm{l}_2} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{r}_2^2}{\mathrm{r}_1^2}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{8}
\end{aligned}$

50859.subject: Physics
50859.text:
A source of sound is moving with a velocity of \( 50 $\mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$\) towards a stationary observer. The
observer measures the frequency of sound as \( 500 $\mathrm{ Hz}$\). The apparent frequency of sound as
heard by the observer when source is moving away from him with the same speed is (Speed
of sound at room temperature \( 350 $\mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$\) )
50859.sol:
Given, velocity of source of sound \( =50 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$\); frequency measured by observer \( =500 $\mathrm{~Hz}$\)
Now, frequency of sound when source is moving towards stationary observer is
\[ f^{\prime}=f$\left(\frac{v}{v-v_{s}}\right) \rightarrow($1) \]
Frequency of sound when source is moving away from the stationary observer is
\[ f^{\prime \prime}=f$\left(\frac{v}{v+v_{s}}\right) \rightarrow($2) \]
Using Eqs. (1) and (2), we have
\[ $\begin{array}{r}$$\frac{f^{\prime}}{f^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{f\left(\frac{v}{v-v_{s}}\right)}{f\left(\frac{v}{v+v_{s}}\right)}$\\ \Rightarrow $\frac{f^{\prime}}{f^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{\left(v+v_{s}\right)}{\left(v-v_{s}\right)} \end{array}$\]
Substitute \( v=350 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$; v_{s}=50 $\mathrm{~ms}^{-}$\)
\[ $\begin{array}{l}$f^{\prime}=500 H z \\ $\frac{500}{f^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{350+50}{350-50}$\\ \Rightarrow $\frac{500}{f^{\prime \prime}}=\frac{400}{300}$\\ \Rightarrow f^{\prime \prime}=$\frac{300 \times 500}{400} \end{array}$\]
Therefore, \( f^{\prime \prime}=375 $\mathrm{~Hz}$\)
Thus, apparent frequency of sound as heard by the observer when source is moving away from him is \( 375 $\mathrm{~Hz}$\).

$M\left(V - V^{'}\right) = mv$

Dividing Eq. (iv) by Eq. (iii), we have

or $V + V^{'} = v$

55271.text: What is IUPAC name of allylamine?
55271.sol:
Allylamine has the structure $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-NH_2}$. The longest carbon chain containing both the double bond and amino group is three carbons. Numbering prioritizes the amino group as the principal functional group, giving it position 1. This places the double bond between carbons 2 and 3, so the parent chain is prop-2-ene. With the amino group at C1, the complete IUPAC name is prop-2-en-1-amine.

Evaluating the options:
A) Propan-1-amine corresponds to $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2}$ (saturated)
B) Prop-2-en-1-amine matches $\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2-NH_2}$
C) Prop-1-en-2-amine would be $\mathrm{CH_2=C(NH_2)-CH_3}$
D) Propan-2-amine is $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)CH_3}$ (saturated)

The correct IUPAC name is $\boxed{B}$.

56804.subject: Chemistry
56804.text: During the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl the product formed at cathode is?
56804.sol:
In the electrolysis of aqueous $\text{NaCl}$, the ions present in the solution are $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$, $\textH^{+}$, and $\text{OH}^{-}$.

At the cathode, reduction occurs. The competing reactions are:
$\text{Na}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{(s)}$ ($E^{{}^{\circ}} = -2.71 \text{ V}$)
$2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}_{(l)} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{H}_{2(g)} + 2\text{OH}^{-}_{(aq)}$ ($E^{{}^{\circ}} = -0.83 \text{ V}$)

Since the standard reduction potential of water is greater than that of sodium ions, water is preferentially reduced at the cathode.

Thus, hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_{2(g)}$) is liberated at the cathode.

Answer: $\text{H}_{2(g)}$

58010.subject: Chemistry
58010.text: Which among the following salts forms basic solution when dissolved in water?
58010.sol:
Determining salt hydrolysis behavior requires analyzing the acid-base character of constituent ions.

Ammonium nitrate ($\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{NO}_3$) derives from weak base $\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}$ and strong acid $\mathrm{HNO}_3$. Its cation hydrolyzes: $\mathrm{NH}_4^+ + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH} + \mathrm{H}^+$, yielding acidic solution.

Sodium carbonate ($\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$) comes from strong base $\mathrm{NaOH}$ and weak acid $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$. Its anion hydrolyzes: $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{HCO}_3^- + \mathrm{OH}^-$, producing basic solution.

Sodium nitrate ($\mathrm{NaNO}_3$) forms from strong acid and strong base; neither ion hydrolyzes, resulting in neutral solution.

Copper(II) sulfate ($\mathrm{CuSO}_4$) originates from weak base $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{OH})_2$ and strong acid. The hydrated copper ion acts as acid: $[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_6]^{2+} + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons [\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_5\mathrm{OH}]^+ + \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+$, giving acidic solution.

Only sodium carbonate yields a basic aqueous solution.

58875.text:
Calculate the molar mass of an element if it forms fcc unit cell structure
[mass of unit cell $=1.8 \times 10^{-22} \mathrm{ g}, \mathrm{ N}_{\mathrm{A}}=6.022 \times 10^{23} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ]
58875.sol:
Molar mass calculation for FCC unit cell

The face-centered cubic structure has $Z = 4$ atoms per unit cell, calculated as $8 \times \frac{1}{8} + 6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4$ atoms.

Given the unit cell mass as $1.8 \times 10^{-22}$ g, the mass per atom is $m = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-22}}{4} = 4.5 \times 10^{-23}$ g.

Using Avogadro's number $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$ mol⁻¹, the molar mass becomes:

$M = m \times N_A = (4.5 \times 10^{-23}) \times (6.022 \times 10^{23}) = 27.099$ g mol⁻¹

The calculated molar mass of $27.1$ g mol⁻¹ corresponds to option A: $27.0$ g mol⁻¹.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

59136.text: Calculate the mole fraction of pure liquid $B$ in solution if total vapour pressure of solution, vapour pressure of pure liquid A and vapour pressure of pure liquid B are $500 \mathrm{mmHg}, 400 \mathrm{ mm} \mathrm{Hg}$ and 575 mm Hg respectively at given temperature.
59136.sol:
To determine the mole fraction of liquid B, Raoult's law is applied to the ideal solution. The total vapor pressure is expressed as $P_{\text{total}} = (1 - X_B) P_A^0 + X_B P_B^0$, given $P_{\text{total}} = 500\,\text{mmHg}$, $P_A^0 = 400\,\text{mmHg}$, and $P_B^0 = 575\,\text{mmHg}$.

$500 = (1 - X_B) \cdot 400 + X_B \cdot 575$

Simplifying this equation results in $100 = 175 X_B$, yielding $X_B = \frac{100}{175} = \frac{4}{7} \approx 0.5714$.

This value corresponds to option B, confirming the mole fraction of B is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

59205.text: Identify the reason for the solubility of polar solute in polar solvent from the following.
options: solute - solute interactions, solute solvent interactions and solvent - solvent interactions are of similar magnitude.

solvent- solvent interactions > solute solvent interactions > solute - solute interactions.
solute - solvent interactions > solute solute interactions > solvent - solvent interactions.
59205.sol:
The solubility of a polar solute in a polar solvent is mainly due to the favorable interactions between the solute and solvent molecules. These interactions are crucial for the dissolution process.
The most appropriate explanation for this is when the solute-solvent interactions are comparable in magnitude to the solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions. This balance allows the solute to dissolve efficiently, as the solvent can break apart the solute molecules while maintaining similar intermolecular forces within the solvent.
Correct answer: (1) Solute-solute interactions, solute-solvent interactions, and solvent-solvent interactions are of similar magnitude. This describes a scenario where the polar solute can easily dissolve in the polar solvent due to similar intermolecular forces being at play in both the solute and the solvent.

60839.text: Let z be the complex number with $\operatorname{Im}(\mathrm{z})=10$ and satisfing $\frac{2 \mathrm{z}-\mathrm{n}}{2 \mathrm{z}+\mathrm{n}}=2 i-1$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$, for some natural number ' n ' then
60839.sol:
The complex number is given by $z = x + 10i$, since $\operatorname{Im}(z) = 10$. Substituting $z$ into the equation:

$\frac{2(x + 10i) - n}{2(x + 10i) + n} = 2i - 1$

Simplify the numerator and denominator:

$\frac{(2x - n) + 20i}{(2x + n) + 20i} = -1 + 2i$

Multiply both sides by the denominator:

$(2x - n) + 20i = (-1 + 2i)((2x + n) + 20i)$

Expand the right-hand side:

$(2x - n) + 20i = -1(2x + n) - 20i + (4x + 2n)i + 40i^2$

Since $i^2 = -1$:

$(2x - n) + 20i = -2x - n - 20i + (4x + 2n)i - 40$

Group real and imaginary parts:

Real: $2x - n = -2x - n - 40$
Imaginary: $20 = -20 + 4x + 2n$

From the real equation:

$2x = -2x - 40 \Rightarrow 4x = -40 \Rightarrow x = -10$

Substitute into the imaginary equation:

$40 = 4(-10) + 2n \Rightarrow 40 = -40 + 2n \Rightarrow 2n = 80 \Rightarrow n = 40$

The values are $n = 40$ and $\operatorname{Re}(z) = -10$, corresponding to option D.

62820.subject: Mathematics
62820.text: The feasible region represented by the constraints $y - 2x \leq 4, x + y \geq 5, x \leq 4, y \geq 2, x, y \geq 0$ is...........
options: a convex bounded region with 4 corner points
a convex bounded region with 5 corner points
62820.sol:
The given constraints are:
$y - 2x \leq 4$
$x + y \geq 5$
$x \leq 4$
$y \geq 2$
$x \geq 0, y \geq 0$

To find the corner points of the feasible region, we solve the boundary equations pairwise and check if the intersection points satisfy all other constraints.

1. Intersection of $y - 2x = 4 and x + y = 5$:
Substituting $y = 5 - x$ into the first equation:
$5 - x - 2x = 4 \Rightarrow 3x = 1 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{3}$
$y = 5 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{14}{3}$
Point: $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{14}{3}\right)$. This satisfies $x \leq 4$ and $y \geq 2$.

2. Intersection of $y - 2x = 4 and x = 4$:
$y - 2(4) = 4 \Rightarrow y = 12$
Point: $(4, 12)$. This satisfies $x + y = 16 \geq 5$ and $y \geq 2$.

3. Intersection of $x = 4 and y = 2$:
Point: $(4, 2)$. This satisfies $y - 2x = 2 - 8 = -6 \leq 4$ and $x + y = 6 \geq 5$.

4. Intersection of $y = 2 and x + y = 5$:
$x + 2 = 5 \Rightarrow x = 3$
Point: $(3, 2)$. This satisfies $y - 2x = 2 - 6 = -4 \leq 4$ and $x \leq 4$.

The constraints $x \geq 0$ and $y \geq 0$ do not form any additional boundary since the minimum values in the region are $x = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and y = 2.

The feasible region is bounded by these four points: $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{14}{3}\right)$, $(4, 12)$, $(4, 2)$, and $(3, 2)$. Since it is formed by the intersection of linear inequalities (half-planes), it is a convex polygon.

Thus, the feasible region is a convex bounded region with 4 corner points.

Answer: a convex bounded region with 4 corner points

64099.text: A radioactive substance, with initial mass $m_0$, has a half-life of $\mathrm{h}$ days. Then its initial decay rate is given by
64099.sol:
Let $\mathrm{m}$ be the mass of substance at time $\mathrm{t}$. Then,
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\mathrm{km} \text{, where } \mathrm{k} > 0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{m}}=-\mathrm{kdt}\end{aligned}$
Integrating on both sides, we get
$\log m=-k t+c$
When $\mathrm{t}=0, \mathrm{ m}=\mathrm{m}_0\therefore \quad \log \mathrm{m}_0=0+\mathrm{c}\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=\log \mathrm{m}_0\therefore \quad \log m=-k t+\log m_0\Rightarrow \log \frac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{m}_0}=-\mathrm{kt}$
When $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{h}, \mathrm{m}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{ m}_0\therefore \quad \log \left(\frac{\frac{1}{2} m_0}{m_0}\right)=-k h\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \log \frac{1}{2}=-\mathrm{kh} \\ & \Rightarrow \log 2=\mathrm{kh}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\frac{\log 2}{\mathrm{ h}}$ ...(i)
Initial decay rate,
$\frac{\mathrm{dm}}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\mathrm{km}_0=\frac{-\mathrm{m}_0}{\mathrm{ h}} \log 2$ ...[From (i)]

64466.text:
The distance between the line
$\bar{r}=3 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}+\hat{k}+\lambda(\hat{i}-2\hat{j})$ and the plane $\bar{r} \cdot(2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=4$ is
64466.sol:
The distance between a line and a plane is determined by their relative orientation. For the line $\bar{r}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}+\lambda(\hat{i}-2\hat{j})$ and the plane $\bar{r}\cdot(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})=4$, the direction vector $\bar{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}$ is perpendicular to the normal vector $\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ since their dot product is zero:

$\bar{b}\cdot\bar{n} = (1)(2)+(-2)(1)+(0)(1)=0$

Thus, the line is parallel to the plane, and the distance equals the perpendicular distance from any point on the line to the plane. Using point $\bar{a}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, compute:

$\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=3\cdot2+(-2)\cdot1+1\cdot1=5$

The magnitude of the normal vector is $|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{6}$.

The distance is then given by:

$D=\frac{|5-4|}{\sqrt{6}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$

This corresponds to option A.

64943.subject: Mathematics
64943.text: In $\triangle ABC$, with the usual notations, $\angle C = 90^{}^{\circ}$, then $\sin(A - B)$ is equal to....
64943.sol:
In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C = 90^{}^{\circ}$.

Using trigonometric ratios in a right-angled triangle:

$\sin A = \dfrac{a}{c}$

$\cos A = \dfrac{b}{c}$

$\sin B = \dfrac{b}{c}$

$\cos B = \dfrac{a}{c}$

Using the expansion formula for $\sin(A - B)$:

$\sin(A - B) = \sin A \cos B - \cos A \sin B$

Substituting the values:

$\sin(A - B) = \left(\dfrac{a}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{a}{c}\right) - \left(\dfrac{b}{c}\right)\left(\dfrac{b}{c}\right)

\sin(A - B) = \dfrac{a^2 - b^2}{c^2}

By Pythagoras theorem in \triangle ABC$, $c^2 = a² + b²$.

Substituting $c^2 = a² + b²$:

$\sin(A - B) = \dfrac{a^2 - b²}{a^2 + b²}$

Answer: $\dfrac{a^2 - b²}{a^2 + b²}$

71243.text: Nearly 80% of nitrogen found in human tissues originate from ____ nitrogen fixation.
71243.sol:
The Haber-Bosch process is an artificial nitrogen fixation process and is the main industrial procedure for the production of ammonia today. The ammonia produced is primarily used to make synthetic fertilizers. It is estimated that nearly $80\%$ of the nitrogen found in human tissues originates from industrial nitrogen fixation.

Answer: industrial

71736.subject: Chemistry
71736.text: Identify the geometry and magnetic behavior of the complex $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$.
71736.sol:
The oxidation state of $\text{Ni}$ in $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$ is $0$.

The electronic configuration of $\text{Ni}(0)$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

Since $\text{CO}$ is a strong field ligand, it causes the pairing of electrons. The two $4s$ electrons are forced into the $3d$ orbitals, resulting in a completely filled $3d^{10}$ configuration.

The empty $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals undergo $sp^3$ hybridization to accommodate the four electron pairs from the four $\text{CO}$ ligands.

Due to $sp^3$ hybridization, the geometry of the complex is tetrahedral.

Since all electrons are paired, the complex is diamagnetic.

Answer: tetrahedral geometry and diamagnetic

72476.subject: Physics
72476.text:
Identify the CORRECT statement on beats
(A) The amplitude of beats is always constant.
(B) Beats are produced when two waves have the same frequency.
(C) Beat frequency is the average of the two source frequencies.
(D) Beats can be produced by the waves having slightly different frequencies and traveling in the opposite directions.
72476.sol:
Beats are produced by the superposition of two waves having slightly different frequencies. The beat frequency is equal to the difference between the frequencies of the two waves, i.e., $f_{beat} = |f_1 - f_2|$.

The amplitude of the resultant wave in a beat pattern varies periodically with time, so it is not constant.

When two waves of slightly different frequencies travel in opposite directions, their superposition at any fixed point in space results in an amplitude that varies periodically with time. This periodic variation in intensity is perceived as beats. Therefore, beats can be produced by waves traveling in opposite directions as long as their frequencies are slightly different.

Answer: (D)

72637.text:
Given below are sentences that use discourse markers/expressions to make them complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker and mark your answer accordingly on the Answer Sheet.

__________, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.
72637.sol:
The sentence requires a discourse marker that introduces a broad or overall statement. 'In general' is used to indicate that a statement is mostly true or true in most situations. It fits perfectly in the context of describing the overall policy of the Government of India. 'Particular' is an adjective and would require 'In' to function as a discourse marker. 'Knowingly' and 'Otherwise' do not fit the context of the sentence.

Thus, the complete sentence is: 'In general, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.'

Answer: In general

78334.subject: Mathematics
78334.text:
For the following two (02) items:
Let $(6 + 10 + 14 + \ldots\text{ up to }m\text{ terms}) = (1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + \ldots\text{ up to }n\text{ terms})$, where $m < 25$ and $n < 25$.

How many values of $m$ are possible?
78334.sol:
The sum of the first $m$ terms of the arithmetic progression $6, 10, 14, \ldots$ is given by:

$S_m = \dfrac{m}{2}[2(6) + (m - 1)4] = \dfrac{m}{2}[12 + 4m - 4] = 2m^2 + 4m$

The sum of the first $n$ terms of the arithmetic progression $1, 3, 5, 7, \ldots$ is given by:

$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2(1) + (n - 1)2] = n^2$

Equating the two sums, we get:

$2m^2 + 4m = n^2$

$2(m^2 + 2m + 1) - 2 = n^2$

$2(m + 1)^2 - n^2 = 2$

Let $u = m + 1$. The equation becomes $2u^2 - n^2 = 2$. This implies that $n$ must be an even number. Let $n = 2v$. Substituting this into the equation yields:

$2u^2 - 4v^2 = 2$

$u^2 - 2v^2 = 1$

This is a standard Pell's equation. The fundamental solution is $u_1 = 3$ and $v_1 = 2$.

For $u_1 = 3$ and $v_1 = 2$, we have $m + 1 = 3 \Rightarrow m = 2$ and $n = 2(2) = 4$. Both $m < 25$ and $n < 25$ are satisfied.

The next solution is generated by $(u_1 + v_1\sqrt{2})^2 = (3 + 2\sqrt{2})^2 = 17 + 12\sqrt{2}$.

Thus, $u_2 = 17$ and $v_2 = 12$, which gives $m + 1 = 17 \Rightarrow m = 16$ and $n = 2(12) = 24$. Both $m < 25$ and $n < 25$ are satisfied.

The third solution is generated by $(3 + 2\sqrt{2})^3 = 99 + 70\sqrt{2}$.

Thus, $u_3 = 99$ and $v_3 = 70$, which gives $m + 1 = 99 \Rightarrow m = 98$ and $n = 2(70) = 140$. This does not satisfy the given conditions $m < 25$ and $n < 25$.

Therefore, the only possible values for $m$ are $2$ and $16$. There are exactly two possible values.

Answer: Two

Microtubules take part in the spindle formation. Mitochondria, vacuoles, and plastids. etc. are membrane-bound structures. The dividing cells possess a large number of mitochondria.

82662.subject: Physics
82662.text:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero.
B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density.
C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation.
D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point.
E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
82662.sol:
Statement A is correct because in electrostatics, the free charges inside a conductor redistribute themselves such that the net electric field inside is zero.

Statement B is incorrect because the electric field at the surface of a charged conductor is given by $E = \dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}$, which directly depends on the surface charge density $\sigma$.

Statement C is correct because, by Gauss's law, since the electric field inside the conductor is zero, the net charge enclosed by any Gaussian surface inside the conductor must be zero. Thus, any excess charge resides entirely on the outer surface.

Statement D is correct because if the electric field had a tangential component, free charges on the surface would experience a force and move, which contradicts the assumption of an electrostatic situation. Hence, the field must be normal to the surface.

Statement E is incorrect because the electric field inside a conductor is zero, which implies that the electrostatic potential is constant throughout the volume of the conductor, but it is not necessarily zero.

Therefore, only statements A, C, and D are correct.

Answer: A, C and D only

83133.subject: Physics
83133.text: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity $u$. When bullet travels $24cm$ through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes $\dfrac{u}{3}$. Then it further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is :
83133.sol:
For the first part of the motion of the bullet into the block, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}{\left(\dfrac{u}{3}\right)}^{2} & = & {u}^{2} - 2a \times 24 \\ & ⇒ & 48a = \dfrac{8{u}^{2}}{9} . . . \left(1\right)\end{cases}$

For the second part of the motion of the bullet through the block, it can be written that

$\begin{cases}0 & = & {\left(\dfrac{u}{3}\right)}^{2} - 2aS \\ & ⇒ & 2aS = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{9} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) to obtain the distance travelled by the bullet during the second part of its motion.

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{2aS}{48a} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{{u}^{2}}{9}}{\dfrac{8{u}^{2}}{9}} \\ & ⇒ & S = 3\end{cases}$

Hence, the total length of the block is given by

$\begin{cases}L & = & \left(3 + 24\right)cm \\ & = & 27cm\end{cases}$

84017.subject: Zoology
84017.text: Silencing of mRNA has been used in producing transgenic plants resistant to
84017.sol: RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defense. This method involves silencing of a specific mRNA due to a complementary ds RNA molecule that binds to and prevents translation of the mRNA (silencing). The source of this complementary RNA could be from an infection by viruses having RNA genome or mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate. Using Agrobacterium vectors, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plant. The introduction of DNA was such that it produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells. These two RNA's being complementary to each other formed a ds RNA that initiated RNAi and thus, silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode. The result was that the parasite could not survive in a transgenic host expressing specific interfering RNA. The transgenic plant, therefore, got itself protected from the parasite.

84156.subject: Zoology
84156.sol:
Frogs are amphibians that can live both on land and in water.

In water, frogs respire through their highly vascularized moist skin. This process is known as cutaneous respiration.

The dissolved oxygen in water diffuses through the skin into the blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses out.

On land, frogs use their buccal cavity, skin, and lungs for respiration.

Answer: skin

85906.subject: Biology
85906.text: Consider a mitochondrion in which the $F_0$ subunit of ATP synthase is mutated, such that it can still passively conduct protons but is mechanically uncoupled from the $F_1$ subunit. If such a mitochondrion is provided with succinate, ADP, and $P_i$ in aerobic conditions, the correct outcome based on chemiosmotic theory is:
options: No oxygen consumption and no ATP synthesis.
Continuous oxygen consumption and normal ATP synthesis.
Continuous oxygen consumption and no ATP synthesis.
Rapid initial oxygen consumption that plateaus at a low rate and normal ATP synthesis.
85906.sol:
Succinate acts as an electron donor to the electron transport chain (ETC) via Complex II. In aerobic conditions, electrons flow through the ETC to oxygen, which acts as the terminal electron acceptor, leading to continuous oxygen consumption.

As electrons move through the ETC, protons are pumped from the mitochondrial matrix into the intermembrane space, creating a proton gradient. Since the mutated $F_0$ subunit can still passively conduct protons, the protons will flow back into the matrix, dissipating the proton gradient. This continuous dissipation prevents the build-up of a high proton motive force that would otherwise inhibit the ETC, allowing oxygen consumption to proceed continuously.

However, because the $F_0$ subunit is mechanically uncoupled from the $F_1$ subunit, the energy from the proton flow is not transmitted to $F_1$. Consequently, the conformational changes required to synthesize ATP from ADP and $P_i$ do not occur, resulting in no ATP synthesis.

This scenario is functionally identical to the effect of an uncoupling agent, where the ETC and oxygen consumption continue without the production of ATP.

Answer: Continuous oxygen consumption and no ATP synthesis.

86738.subject: Physics
86738.text: Physicist Luis Alvarez and his collaborators hypothesised that the extinction of dinosaurs was due to the impact of an asteroid with the Earth. They estimated the mass and the radius of the asteroid to be about $2 \times 10^{15}$ kg and $10$ km respectively. Take the mass of the Earth to be $6 \times 10^{24}$ kg. The gravitational acceleration (in SI units) of the Earth due to the asteroid just before the impact would be of the order
86738.sol:
The gravitational force exerted by the asteroid on the Earth is given by Newton's law of gravitation:

$F = \dfrac{G M_a M_e}{r^2}$

where $M_a$ is the mass of the asteroid, $M_e$ is the mass of the Earth, and $r$ is the distance between their centers. Just before impact, $r = R_e + R_a \approx R_e$, where $R_e = 6.4 \times 10^6$ m is the radius of the Earth.

The acceleration of the Earth due to this force is:

$a_e = \dfrac{F}{M_e} = \dfrac{G M_a}{r^2}$

Substituting the standard value of $G$ and the given mass of the asteroid:

$a_e = \dfrac{6.67 \times 10^{-11} \times 2 \times 10^{15}}{(6.4 \times 10^6)^2}$

$a_e = \dfrac{1.334 \times 10^5}{4.096 \times 10^{13}} \approx 3.25 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m/s}^2$

The order of magnitude of the acceleration is $10^{-9}$.

89931.text: If ${5}^{97}$ is divided by $52$, then the remainder obtained is
89931.sol:
We know that, ${5}^{4} = 625 = 52 \times 12 + 1$

$⇒ {5}^{4} = 52\lambda + 1$ , where $\lambda$ is a positive integer.

$⇒ {\left({5}^{4}\right)}^{24} = {\left(52\lambda + 1\right)}^{24}$

$= {C}_{0} 24 {\left(52\lambda\right)}^{24} + {C}_{1}{\left(52\lambda\right)}^{23} + {C}_{2} 24 {\left(52\lambda\right)}^{22} 24 + \ldots + {C}_{23}\left(52\lambda\right) + {C}_{24} 24 24$ (by binomial theorem)

$⇒ {5}^{96} = 52\left[{C}_{0} 24 {52}^{23}{\lambda}^{24} + {C}_{1}{52}^{23}{\lambda}^{22} 24 + \ldots + {C}_{23}\lambda 24\right] + 1$

$= \left(amultipleof52\right) + 1$

On multiplying both sides by $5$ , we get

${5}^{97} = {5}^{96} ⋅ 5 = 5\left(amultipleof52\right) + 5$

Hence, the required remainder is $5$.

90085.text: The equation of the circle which passes through the points $A  \left(0,5\right)$ and $B  \left(6,1\right)$ and whose centre lies on the line $12x + 5y = 25$ is
90085.sol:
Centre $C$ of the required circle lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining $\left(0,5\right) \text{ and } \left(6,1\right)$

the midpoint of line segment joining $A$ & $B$ is $\left(3,3\right) = D$



Slope of $AB$ is $- \dfrac{2}{3}$

Slope of $DC$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒$ equation of $DC$ is $3x - 2y - 3 = 0$

$C$ is the point of intersection of $3x - 2y - 3 = 0$ and $12x + 5y = 25 ⇒ C = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}, 1\right)$

Radius $= AC = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{9} + 16} = \dfrac{13}{3}$

$⇒$ equation of the circle is ${\left(x - \dfrac{5}{3}\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2} = {\left(\dfrac{13}{3}\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2} + 3{y}^{2} - 10x - 6y - 45 = 0$

94268.text: A lens is made of flint glass (refractive index = $1. 5$). When the lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1. 25$, the focal length
94268.sol:
Lens-maker's formula is given by

$\dfrac{1}{f} = \left({}_{a}{\mu}_{g} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}\right) \ldots \left(i\right)$

If the lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index ${\mu}_{1}$ then

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({}_{l}{\mu}_{g} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}\right) \ldots \left(ii\right)$

Here, ${}_{l}{\mu}_{g}$is refractive index of glass w.r.t liquid

Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we have

$\dfrac{{f}_{1}}{f} = \dfrac{\left({}_{a}{\mu}_{g} - 1\right)}{\left({}_{l}{\mu}_{g} - 1\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}_{1}}{f} = \left(\dfrac{1.5 - 1}{\dfrac{1.5}{1.25} - 1}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{{f}_{1}}{f} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 1.25}{0.25} = 2.5 ⇒ {f}_{1} = ( 2.5 )f$

Hence, focal length increases by a factor of 2.5.

100047.subject: Physics
100047.text: $\mathrm{R}=65 \pm 1 \Omega \mathrm{L}, \mathrm{l}=5 \pm 0.1 \mathrm{~mm}$ and $\mathrm{d}=10 \pm 0.5 \mathrm{~mm}$. Find error in calculation of resistivity.
100047.sol:
Given that, $\mathrm{R}=65 \Omega, \Delta \mathrm{R}=1 \Omega, \mathrm{l}=5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$, $\Delta \mathrm{l}=0.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{~d}=10 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}, \Delta \mathrm{d}=0.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}$
$\because$ Resistivity, $\rho=\frac{R A}{l}$
or $\quad \rho=\frac{\mathrm{R} \pi(\mathrm{d} / 2)^2}{\mathrm{l}}=\frac{\pi \mathrm{Rd}^2}{4 \mathrm{l}}$
$\begin{array}{ll}\therefore & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}}+2 \frac{\Delta \mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{l}}{\mathrm{l}} \\ \therefore & \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=\frac{1}{65}+2\left(\frac{0.5 \times 10^{-3}}{10 \times 10^{-3}}\right)+\frac{0.1 \times 10^{-3}}{5 \times 10^{-3}}\end{array}$
or $\quad \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}=0.0153+0.1+0.02$
or $\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \approx 0.1353$
So, error in calculation of resistivity is
$13.5 \% \approx 13 \%$.

101438.subject: Physics
101438.text: Time period of pendulum, on a satellite orbiting the earth, is
101438.sol:
On an artificial satellite orbiting the earth the acceleration is given by $\frac{G M}{R^2}$ towards the centre of the earth. Now for a body of mass $m$ on the satellite the graviational force due to earth is $\frac{G M m}{R^2}$ towards the centre of the earth. Let the reaction force on the surface of the satellite be $N$, then
$\frac{G M m}{R^2}-N=m\left(\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \quad N=0$
That is on the satellite there is a state of weightlessness or $g=0$
$\therefore \quad$ The time period of the simple pendulum,
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}=\infty$

103663.subject: Physics
103663.text: A circular loop is formed by joining two wire arcs, Arc 1 and Arc 2. Arc 1 subtends an angle of $60^{\circ}$ at the centre of the loop, while Arc 2 subtends $300^{\circ}$. A steady current enters the loop at one junction of the arcs and leaves at the other junction. It is observed that the magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre due to Arc 1 is exactly twice the magnitude of the magnetic field due to Arc 2. What is the ratio of the resistance of Arc 1 to the resistance of Arc 2 ($R_1 : R_2$)?
103663.sol:
The magnetic field at the centre of a circular arc subtending an angle $\theta$ is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R} \times \dfrac{\theta}{360^{\circ}}$.

For Arc 1 ($\theta_1 = 60^{\circ}$):
$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{2R} \times \dfrac{60^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{12R}$

For Arc 2 ($\theta_2 = 300^{\circ}$):
$B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I_2}{2R} \times \dfrac{300^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}} = \dfrac{5\mu_0 I_2}{12R}$

It is given that $B_1 = 2B_2$. Substituting the expressions:
$\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1}{12R} = 2 \times \left( \dfrac{5\mu_0 I_2}{12R} \right)$
$\Rightarrow I_1 = 10 I_2$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = 10$

Since the two arcs are connected in parallel between the entry and exit junctions, the potential difference across them is the same.
$V_1 = V_2 \Rightarrow I_1 R_1 = I_2 R_2$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{I_2}{I_1} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

Thus, the ratio of their resistances is $1 : 10$.

Answer: $1 : 10$

103916.subject: Physics
103916.text: A circular coil of $50$ turns and cross-sectional area $2\text{ m}^2$ is placed such that its plane is perpendicular to a time-varying magnetic field. The magnetic field changes with time according to the relation $B(t) = 0.2t^2 - 0.05t$ (where $B$ is in tesla and $t$ is in seconds). The magnitude of the induced emf in the coil at $t = 2\text{ s}$ will be:
103916.sol:
The magnetic flux linked with the coil is given by $\Phi = NBA\cos\theta$.

Since the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the angle between the area vector and the magnetic field is $\theta = 0^{\circ}$. Thus, $\cos(0^{\circ}) = 1$.

Substituting the given values:

$\Phi(t) = 50 \times 2 \times (0.2t^2 - 0.05t)$

$\Phi(t) = 100(0.2t^2 - 0.05t) = 20t^2 - 5t$

According to Faraday's law, the magnitude of the induced emf is $|e| = \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$.

Differentiating the flux equation with respect to time:

$|e| = \dfrac{d}{dt}(20t^2 - 5t) = 40t - 5$

At $t = 2\text{ s}$, the magnitude of the induced emf is:

$|e| = 40(2) - 5 = 80 - 5 = 75\text{ V}$

Answer: $75\text{ V}$

103948.text: Two solenoidal coils, $P$ and $Q$, are connected in different circuits. Coil $Q$ is wound with twice the total number of turns as coil $P$, has twice the length, and half the cross-sectional area of coil $P$. If the current flowing through coil $Q$ is twice that in coil $P$, the ratio of the magnetic energy stored in coil $P$ to that in coil $Q$ ($U_P : U_Q$) is
103948.sol:
The self-inductance of a solenoid is given by $L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}$.

Let the parameters for coil $P$ be $N_P$, $l_P$, and $A_P$.
For coil $Q$, we are given $N_Q = 2N_P$, $l_Q = 2l_P$, and $A_Q = \dfrac{A_P}{2}$.

The ratio of their self-inductances is:
$\dfrac{L_Q}{L_P} = \left(\dfrac{N_Q}{N_P}\right)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{A_Q}{A_P}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{l_P}{l_Q}\right)$

$\dfrac{L_Q}{L_P} = (2)^2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 4 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 1$

Thus, $L_P = L_Q$.

The magnetic energy stored in an inductor is $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L i^2$.
Since $L$ is the same for both coils, $U \propto i^2$.

Given that $i_Q = 2i_P$, the ratio of stored energy is:
$\dfrac{U_P}{U_Q} = \left(\dfrac{i_P}{i_Q}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Therefore, the ratio $U_P : U_Q$ is $1:4$.

Answer: $1:4$

104477.subject: Physics
104477.text: An object is placed at a distance of $20\text{ cm}$ in front of a combination of two thin lenses in contact. A real image is formed at a distance of $30\text{ cm}$ from the combination. The first lens is equiconvex with a refractive index of $1.5$ and a radius of curvature of $30\text{ cm}$ for both surfaces. If the second lens is plano-convex with a radius of curvature of $12\text{ cm}$ for its curved surface, what is the refractive index of the material of the second lens?
104477.sol:
Using the thin lens formula for the combination to find its equivalent focal length $F$:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{F}$
$\dfrac{1}{+30} - \dfrac{1}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{F}$
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{5}{60} = \dfrac{1}{12}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

Using the lens maker's formula to find the focal length of the first equiconvex lens $f_1$:
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (\mu_1 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{-R_1}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5 - 1)\left(\dfrac{2}{30}\right) = 0.5 \times \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

The equivalent focal length of two thin lenses in contact is given by:
$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{f_2}$
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{5 - 2}{60} = \dfrac{3}{60} = \dfrac{1}{20}\text{ cm}^{-1}$

Using the lens maker's formula for the second plano-convex lens to find its refractive index $\mu_2$:
$\dfrac{1}{f_2} = (\mu_2 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{20} = (\mu_2 - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{12}\right)$
$\mu_2 - 1 = \dfrac{12}{20} = 0.6$
$\mu_2 = 1.6$

Answer: $1.6$

104913.text: An energy of 68.0 eV is required to excite a hydrogen-like atom in its second Bohr energy level to third energy level the charge of nucleus is Ze . The wavelength of a radiation required to eject the electron from first orbit to infinity is
104913.sol:
Given, $n_1=2, n_2=3$ and $\Delta E=68 \mathrm{eV}$
The difference in energies of two orbits
$\Delta E=13.6 Z^2\left[\frac{1}{n_1^2}-\frac{1}{n_2^2}\right]$
where, $n_1 \lt n_2$
$\begin{aligned} 68 & =13.6 Z^2\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right] \\ & =13.6 Z^2\left[\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right] \\ & =13.6 Z^2\left[\frac{9-4}{36}\right] \\ & =13.6 Z^2 \times \frac{5}{36}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad Z^2 & =\frac{68 \times 36}{13.6 \times 5}=36 \\ Z & =6\end{aligned}$
$\because$ Wavelength of photon, $\frac{1}{\lambda}=Z^2 R\left[\frac{1}{n_1^2}-\frac{1}{n_2^2}\right]$
$n_1=1$ and $n_2=\infty$
$\frac{1}{\lambda}=6^2 \times R\left[\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right]=36 R$
$\therefore \quad \lambda=\frac{1}{36 R}=\frac{1}{36 \times 1.097 \times 10^7}$
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{10^{-7}}{39.5} \mathrm{~m} \\ & =0.025 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m} \\ & =2.5 \mathrm{~nm}\end{aligned}$

105581.subject: Physics
105581.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If the distance of a point source of monochromatic light from a photoelectric metal surface is doubled, the stopping potential of the emitted photoelectrons remains unchanged.

Reason (R): The stopping potential depends only on the frequency of incident light and the nature of the material, and is independent of the intensity of light.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
105581.sol:
For a point source of light, the intensity $I$ at a distance $r$ follows the inverse square law ($I \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}$).

When the distance is doubled, the intensity of the light falling on the metal surface becomes one-fourth of its initial value. However, the frequency of the incident monochromatic light remains unchanged.

According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy and hence the stopping potential ($V_0 = \dfrac{h\nu - \phi_0}{e}$) depend only on the frequency of the incident light and the work function of the material. They are completely independent of the intensity of the incident light.

Therefore, the stopping potential remains unchanged. Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) provides the correct explanation for (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

117803.subject: Chemistry
117803.text: The nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) is classified as an ambidentate ligand. Which of the following statements correctly describes the reason for this classification?
options: It possesses two different donor atoms but coordinates to the central metal ion through only one at a time.
It possesses two donor atoms and coordinates through both of them simultaneously.
It coordinates to the central metal ion in a way that forms a stable chelate ring.
It acts as a bridging ligand by coordinating to two different central metal ions simultaneously.
117803.sol:
An ambidentate ligand is a unidentate ligand that contains more than one coordinating atom but coordinates through only one donor atom at a time.

The nitrite ion ($NO_2^-$) has two potential donor atoms: nitrogen and oxygen. It can bind to a metal ion either through the nitrogen atom (forming a nitro complex) or through the oxygen atom (forming a nitrito complex), but not both simultaneously.

Coordinating through two atoms simultaneously or forming a chelate ring is characteristic of bidentate or polydentate ligands, not ambidentate ligands.

Answer: It possesses two different donor atoms but coordinates to the central metal ion through only one at a time.

121596.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes exhibit a distinct dikaryophase $(n+n)$ during their sexual reproduction.

Reason (R): In these fungi, plasmogamy is not immediately followed by karyogamy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is not correct
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is not correct but Reason (R) is correct
121596.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct: During sexual reproduction in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, an intervening dikaryotic stage (dikaryophase) occurs, where cells contain two distinct nuclei $(n+n)$.

Reason (R) is correct and explains Assertion (A): The dikaryophase arises specifically because the fusion of protoplasms (plasmogamy) is not immediately followed by the fusion of nuclei (karyogamy). This delay leaves two haploid nuclei per cell, creating the dikaryon.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

121774.subject: Botany
121774.text: What does the zygote develop into in bryophytes?
121774.sol: Bryophytes include the various mosses and liverworts that are found commonly growing in moist shaded areas in the hills. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom because these plants can live in soil but are dependent on water for sexual reproduction. They usually occur in damp, humid and shaded localities. They play an important role in plant succession on bare rocks/soil. The plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. They lack true roots, stems or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures. The main plant body of the bryophyte is haploid. It produces gametes, hence is called a gametophyte. The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular. The male sex organ is called antheridium. They produce biflagellate antherozoids. The female sex organ called archegonium is flask-shaped and produces a single egg. The antherozoids are released into water where they come in contact with archegonium. An antherozoid fuses with the egg to produce the zygote. <mark>Zygotes do not undergo reduction division immediately. They produce a multicellular body called a sporophyte.</mark> The sporophyte is not free-living but attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it. Some cells of the sporophyte undergo reduction division (meiosis) to produce haploid spores. These spores germinate to produce gametophyte.

123609.subject: Botany
123609.text: What is the purpose of the kinetochores in mitosis?
options: To align the chromosomes along the metaphase plate
To serve as the site of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes
To initiate the condensation of chromosomal material
123609.sol: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores. These structures serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres (formed by the spindle fibres) to the chromosomes that are moved into position at the centre of the cell. hence, the metaphase is characterised by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate

124069.sol: Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere.

125891.subject: Botany
125891.text: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as an example of a water-pollinated plant?
125891.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. As against this, you would recall that water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. It is believed, particularly for some bryophytes and pteridophytes, that their distribution is limited because of the need for water for the transport of male gametes and fertilisation. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Vallisneria and Hydrilla which grow in fresh water and several marine sea-grasses such as Zostera. Not all aquatic plants use water for pollination. In a majority of aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the level of water and are pollinated by insects or wind as in most of the land plants. In Vallisneria, the female flower reach the surface of water by the long stalk and the male flowers or pollen grains are released on to the surface of water.

127780.subject: Botany
127780.text:
Identify the correct sequence of the steps involved in the process of decomposition:
A. Humification
B. Catabolism
C. Fragmentation
D. Mineralisation
E. Leaching

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
127780.sol:
According to NCERT, the important steps in the process of decomposition are fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, and mineralisation.

First, detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles in a process called fragmentation (C).

Next, by the process of leaching (E), water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

Then, bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances through catabolism (B).

During decomposition in the soil, humification (A) leads to the accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance called humus.

Finally, the humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occurs by the process of mineralisation (D).

Thus, the correct sequence is C $\rightarrow$ E $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ D.

Answer: C $\rightarrow$ E $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ D

128296.subject: Zoology
128296.text: What is the function of Vasopressin hormone?
options: Stimulation of resorption of water and electrolytes
128296.sol: FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles in females. MSH acts on the melanocytes (melanin containing cells) and regulates pigmentation of the skin. Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction. In females, it stimulates a vigorous contraction of uterus at the time of child birth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland. Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules and thereby reduces loss of water through urine (diuresis). Hence, it is also called as antidiuretic hormone (ADH).

128381.subject: Zoology
128381.text: What is the structure in the ovary that secretes mainly progesterone?
128381.sol: Females have a pair of ovaries located in the abdomen (Figure 19.1). Ovary is the primary female sex organ which produces one ovum during each menstrual cycle. In addition, ovary also produces two groups of steroid hormones called estrogen and progesterone. Ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues. The estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted to a structure called corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone. Estrogens produce wide ranging actions such as stimulation of growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, development of growing ovarian follicles, appearance of female secondary sex characters, mammary gland development, and regulation of female sexual behaviour. Endocrine cells present in different parts of the gastro-intestinal tract secrete four major peptide hormones, namely gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin (CCK) and gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP). Gastrin acts on the gastric glands and stimulates the secretion of hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen. Secretin acts on the exocrine pancreas and stimulates secretion of water and bicarbonate ions. CCK acts on both pancreas and gall bladder and stimulates the secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice, respectively

128958.subject: Zoology
128958.text: Identify the correct statement with respect to the following diagram.

A is a atrio-ventricular node (AVN) present in the right upper corner of the right atrium.
C is Bundle of His emerging from Sino-atrial nodes (SAN).
128958.sol: The entire heart is made of cardiac muscles. The walls of ventricles are much thicker than that of the atria. A specialised cardiac musculature called the nodal tissue is also distributed in the heart . A patch of this tissue is present in the right upper corner of the right atrium called the sino-atrial node (SAN). Another mass of this tissue is seen in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum called the atrio-ventricular node (AVN). A bundle of nodal fibres, atrio- ventricular bundle (AV bundle) continues from the AVN which passes through the atrio-ventricular septa to emerge on the top of the inter- ventricular septum and immediately divides into a right and left bundle. These branches give rise to minute fibres throughout the ventricular musculature of the respective sides and are called purkinje fibres. These fibres alongwith right and left bundles are known as bundle of His.
